bridges.description: Show that historical Bibles sometimes attribute non-original wording to Jesus.
Show that a recoverable ancestor need not reproduce the autograph.
Show that some viable variants materially affect interpretation.
Explain why uncertainty challenged Ehrman’s former inspiration view.
Show that variants are not misquotations because wording and message remain recoverable.
Show that distributed transmission preserves readings without central control.
Distinguish raw totals from meaningful viable variants and message continuity.
Show that perfect copies or unanimous certainty are not required.
